results.note: persist_board (pipeline.py:559-596) is one generic loop over run.indicators with no per-category branch; the added test asserts the function's source contains no `_active_addresses`/`_mvrv`/`_exchange_flow`/`_staking` special-casing and persists all three categories through it.
Drives heartbeat.main() end to end and asserts exactly 70 of the 71 registered cells (every cell except sol_active_addresses) are persisted in one run with exactly one success ping.

run_scheduled_board() (pipeline.py:534-545) calls run_all_assets() unconditionally, which still invokes the slow real fetcher for SOL active addresses (_fetch_asset_active_addresses -> solana_rpc.fetch_sol_active_addresses, confirmed as the multi-hour block-enumeration fetch at ingest/fetchers/solana_rpc.py:332-357) and only filters the SOL key out of the result dict afterward. The expensive fetch still executes inside the 10-minute ingest.yml job before being discarded — the split cadence this gate decided is not actually achieved. No test catches this because every test substitutes a fast fake for _fetch_asset_active_addresses across all assets including SOL (tests/test_persist_board.py:177-181, monkeypatched at line 1142-1144), masking production behavior.

Forces an ETH MVRV fetch failure and asserts it persists as an Error row while btc_rsi (technical), btc_funding_rate (derivatives), btc_active_addresses and sol_staking (on-chain) all still persist successfully in the same run.

Pre-existing tests, still exercised: a board with one ERROR-status cell still pings success once persistence completes (test_heartbeat.py:112), while a raised exception during persist pings the /fail endpoint (test_heartbeat.py:80, test_failed_run_pings_the_failure_endpoint_rather_than_staying_silent).

Calls heartbeat.main() (the real module-level entry point matching `python -m ingest.heartbeat` in ingest.yml), which is wired through run_ingestion -> run_pipeline -> persist_board -> persist_datapoint; only the network-touching fetchers are substituted, the call chain itself is the production wiring.
Calls heartbeat.main_sol_active_addresses() (the entry point invoked by sol-active-addresses.yml) end to end and asserts it persists exactly one sol_active_addresses row and pings once.

ingest.yml still declares timeout-minutes: 10 and runs `python -m ingest.heartbeat` (main() -> run_scheduled_board()), but per the C3 defect that path still performs the ~2.5-hour real SOL active-addresses fetch before discarding the result, so the actual scheduled job would overrun its own timeout — the workflow does not actually achieve the isolation it was split off to guarantee.

New dedicated workflow: cron '43 3 * * 0' (weekly), timeout-minutes: 210 (comfortably above the ~2.5h fetch), runs `main_sol_active_addresses()` which (pipeline.py:548-556) fetches only sol_active_addresses — correctly isolated from the rest of the board.

note: Two of nine criteria fail on a real, verifiable defect: run_scheduled_board() still calls run_all_assets(), which invokes the real slow SOL active-addresses fetcher and only discards its result afterward — the 10-minute ingest.yml job still performs the ~2.5-hour Helius fetch internally, defeating the split-cadence decision this story exists to implement. This is masked in every test because the fake fetcher substituted for _fetch_asset_active_addresses is fast for all assets including SOL, so no test observes production timing behavior. The rest of the persistence/heartbeat wiring (single persist_board path, per-cell failure isolation, ERROR-vs-raised-exception distinction, both entry points wired end to end) is genuinely implemented and tested.
